newsitem.title: USA: Invesco to buy AIM for $1.6 bln - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Invesco to buy AIM for $1.6 bln - WSJ.

text.p: British fund management group Invesco has agreed to buy AIM Management Group Inc of the United States for $1.6 billion, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.

The newspaper quoted "people familiar with the matter " as saying Invesco will pay $1.1 billion in stock and $500 million in cash for AIM in what it described as the largest purchase of a U.S. mutual fund company by a foreign fund group.
It said the boards of directors had approved the deal but the investors had yet to vote on it.
The new company, to be called Amvesco, would have about $150 billion under management, it said.
The newspaper said Invesco Chairman Charles Brady would become Amvesco's chairman and chief executive officer and AIM Chairman Charles Bauer its vice chairman.
The companies, which are expected to announce the deal on Monday, declined to comment, it added.
